task.description: Review the Step 2a implementation (commit 9ac7c2eb on branch feature/WF02-batch-4-20260811) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. This batch touches: (1) src/db/partition_conversion.zig -- PAR-05 online partition conversion, a schema/DDL-adjacent operation on the events table; (2) migrations/1150_par06_instance_projections_event_window.sql -- PAR-06 window-column migration plus Store.append()/reconstructBounded() changes; (3) src/engine/pin_resolver.zig -- PIN-01 AC3/AC4/AC5, resolves variable_schema and applies pin_overrides, returns UnresolvedCatalogRef/UnresolvedModuleRef for the explicitly out-of-scope AC1/AC2 branches; (4) migrations/1151_pin02_instance_started_pinned_versions.sql and the src/engine/instance.zig InstanceStore.create() call site -- PIN-02, pin set now recorded in the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload. Determine independently whether any of this is a tenant-data path (new/changed API route, migration, Lua/Wasm host function, secrets code, or response-shaping/lookup-by-ID code) requiring full review against the numbered security invariants, or whether it is out of scope for a PASS-with-note. Do not assume the answer -- this is your determination to make, not ORCH's. Pay particular attention to: tenant isolation in the partition-conversion backfill/swap path (PAR-05), whether the new window columns/migration in PAR-06 could leak cross-tenant data through reconstruction, and whether PIN-01/PIN-02's variable_schema and pin_overrides resolution paths enforce tenant scoping when looking up catalog/schema entries by reference.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit determination of tenant-data-path status for each of the 4 changed files/areas
Full review against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md for any area determined in-scope
PASS with one-line note for any area determined out-of-scope, with the reasoning stated
Any invariant violation found is a FAIL with specific invariant number and file:line cited, not a vague concern
Any NEW incidental security-adjacent finding is filed as its own ISS + GitHub issue per core-directives.md, not silently noted only in this handoff

result.summary: 4 areas independently assessed for tenant-data-path status. (1) PAR-05 partition_conversion.zig: IS a tenant-data path (DDL/migration-adjacent, operates on the per-tenant events table) but is a scheduler/admin tool with no API route exposing it in this diff -- reviewed against INV-1/INV-7/INV-8, all satisfied (identifier interpolation in countRowsInTable() is guarded against embedded quotes and sourced only from plat_partition_catalog, matching partition_attach.zig's existing convention; inverse-rename rollback on row-count mismatch is correct). PASS. (2) PAR-06 migration 1150 + Store.append()/reconstruction.zig: IS a tenant-data path (migration + reconstruction read path). Migration correctly guards the public pass via to_regclass() per the established per-tenant-table convention (1149's precedent). reconstruction.zig's new eventWindowForInstanceInTx()/bounded queries correctly omit an explicit tenant_id predicate, consistent with every other query in that file and with the current schema (instance_projections' tenant_id column was dropped by GBL-084; isolation is search_path-only in SCHEMA mode) -- INV-1 satisfied for the LIVE path. INCIDENTAL FINDING (filed, not a gate failure): Store.reconstructBounded() in store.zig is unreferenced dead code that duplicates this logic with a DIFFERENT (inconsistent) tenant_id-parameter approach -- filed as ISS-0675/GH-716 (MINOR, maintenance hazard, not currently reachable). PASS (with incidental filing). (3)+(4) PIN-01 pin_resolver.zig (AC3/AC4/AC5) + PIN-02 migration 1151 + instance.zig call site: IS a tenant-data path (modifies the live POST /api/v1/instances handler). Migration 1151 correctly guards the public pass (to_regclass on event_type_registry, matching 1149's precedent). PIN-02's payload serialisation (serialisePinnedVersions) is fine -- INV-7 not implicated (no SQL). BUT: INV-1 FAIL. pin_resolver.zig:192-199 (resolveServiceCatalogRef(), called unconditionally by resolve() for every SERVICE_TASK node, which runs unconditionally from instance.zig's InstanceStore.create() Step d.5 on the live create-instance path) issues a query filtering on owner_tenant_id = bpm_effective_tenant_id(). bpm_effective_tenant_id() is a SQL function that migrations/028_adp02_tenant_scope_persistence.sql defined for the retired LEGACY_RLS model and that migrations/GBL-116_tnt07_rls_cleanup.sql, GBL-123_rls_removal.sql, GBL-130_iss503_guard_tenant_type_scope.sql, and GBL-131_iss0100_guard_tc_slug_scope.sql all DROP FUNCTION -- real, applied migrations per migrationOrder()'s GBL- +1000 offset, not an abandoned branch. In any fully-migrated environment the function does not exist: every instance-start with a resolvable SERVICE_TASK service_id fails with Postgres 42883, surfaced as an untyped HTTP 500. Independently, even if the function existed, src/db/pool.zig's applyRequestStorageRouting() only sets bpm.tenant_id in LEGACY_RLS mode (pool.zig:279-282) -- SCHEMA mode, the current target architecture, never sets it (pool.zig:298 comment: RLS is inactive in tenant schemas), so the predicate could not correctly scope by tenant even if resurrected. The design doc (src/design/pin-01-dependency-version-resolution.md line 269-272) claims this reuses SVC-01's existing tenant-visibility rule verbatim -- it does not: the actual SVC-01 implementation, src/repository/service_catalog.zig's getServiceForTenant() (service_catalog.zig:292), correctly uses a bound owner_tenant_id = $2::uuid parameter, and src/definition/service_scope_validator.zig (SVC-03) compares owner_tenant_id against an explicit tenant_id parameter in application code. PinResolver.ResolutionInput (pin_resolver.zig:58-63) has no tenant_id field at all, so resolveServiceCatalogRef() had no bound parameter available and reached for the wrong, now-removed mechanism instead. Filed as ISS-0674/GH-715 (BLOCKER).

issues.description: INV-1 FAIL: src/engine/pin_resolver.zig:197 (resolveServiceCatalogRef, inside PinResolver.resolve(), called from src/engine/instance.zig's InstanceStore.create() Step d.5) filters service_catalog by owner_tenant_id = bpm_effective_tenant_id(), a SQL function dropped by migrations/GBL-116_tnt07_rls_cleanup.sql (order 1116), GBL-123_rls_removal.sql (order 1123), GBL-130_iss503_guard_tenant_type_scope.sql (order 1130), and GBL-131_iss0100_guard_tc_slug_scope.sql (order 1131) as part of the platform's LEGACY_RLS-to-SCHEMA cutover. Breaks every SERVICE_TASK instance-start in a fully-migrated environment (Postgres 42883, surfaced as untyped HTTP 500) and, even if the function were resurrected, would not correctly tenant-scope under SCHEMA mode since src/db/pool.zig only sets the bpm.tenant_id session variable this function reads in LEGACY_RLS mode (pool.zig:277-282 vs. 284-298). Filed as ISS-0674, GitHub issue #715. Fix: add tenant_id to PinResolver.ResolutionInput, thread it from instance.zig's existing request-tenant context, and bind it as $2::uuid, mirroring src/repository/service_catalog.zig's getServiceForTenant() (service_catalog.zig:292) which already implements this correctly.

Incidental finding (not a gate failure -- code is unreferenced): src/event_store/store.zig's Store.reconstructBounded() (PAR-06) is dead code, not called anywhere in src/ or tests/, duplicating src/engine/reconstruction.zig's live eventWindowForInstanceInTx()/reconstructInstance() bounded-reconstruction logic with a DIFFERENT tenant-scoping approach (an explicit tenant_id parameter/predicate the live path does not have and does not need under the current schema). Maintenance hazard: a future caller could wire up the dead function instead of the live one and introduce inconsistent tenant-scoping behavior between two paths meant to do the same thing. Filed as ISS-0675, GitHub issue #716.

result.next_action: Route to BACKEND-DEV for rework: add tenant_id to PinResolver.ResolutionInput / resolveServiceCatalogRef(), bind it as $2::uuid against service_catalog.owner_tenant_id (mirroring ServiceCatalog.getServiceForTenant()), and remove/replace the bpm_effective_tenant_id() reference. Re-submit to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) before TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) may start. PAR-05 and PAR-06 (as implemented) do not need rework -- only PIN-01's resolveServiceCatalogRef() is blocking.
